pr_title: Report GREEN status when FileSettingsService is stopped
pr_body:
When the `FileSettingsService` is inactive, its health indicator should report `GREEN` because it is successfully doing nothing.

Fixes #117591.

**Build Scans:**

- [elasticsearch-pull-request #42568 / part-1](https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/s/iqyjqbiyngji2)

I've run it 1,081 times locally and never observed this failure. The symptom is that the sequence of calls to the `FileSettingsHealthIndicatorService` is not precisely what it's expecting, but actually the observed sequence is acceptable.

It might make more sense just to relax the test case and get it un-muted than to try to get to the bottom of what might be a harmless race condition.

Moving to low risk because I think this is a race in the test case or watcher thread logic that would occur only when multiple file updates occur in rapid succession, which doesn't happen in production (and even if it did, it would succeed >99% of the time according to the failure rates in this issue's description).

Discussed at the fix-it meeting today. It appears that the "failure" behaviour is actually valid, and the appropriate thing to do would be to back off on the assertions to allow this behaviour, then unmute the test.
Update: it makes more sense that the health status is guaranteed to be `GREEN` when the file settings service isn't running. I've updated the logic and the tests accordingly in #118182.

Putting back to `medium-risk` because this is a legit bug in the health indicator.

If something goes wrong (making the status `YELLOW`) and then the `FileSettingsService` is stopped, the health indicator stays `YELLOW` forever despite everything working as expected. In this scenario, the health should go `GREEN`.

review_comments: I got tired of worrying about mixing and matching the states of these fields when they're changed independently. Now they're all just protected by `synchronized`.
